sources.title: Dystopia 1.4.1 dedicated server setup guide - status, kick <name>, kickid <userid>, say <string>, banid <time> <SteamID or UserID> [kick], removeid, writeid, listid, rcon_password, -port (TCP = RCON)
Dystopia 1.4.1 Server Setup Guide: Hosted on GitHub :: Dystopia General Discussions
Game-Server-Configs/Dystopia/server.cfg - rcon_password, exec banned_user.cfg ("Server banlist based on user steam ID"), exec banned_ip.cfg, writeid, writeip
LinuxGSM dysserver/_default.cfg - appid 17585, engine "source", -game dystopia, port 27015, servercfgdir ${systemdir}/cfg
Dystopia Dedicated Server - AppID 17585 (type Tool) - SteamDB
Complete HL2DM Console Commands/CVARs LIST - Source SDK 2013 baseline (kick "Kick a player by name.", kickid "Kick a player by userid or uniqueid, with a message.", banid, addip, listid, motdfile)

Source Dedicated Server Console Commands (cvarlist dump) - removeid "Remove a user ID from the ban list.", writeid "Writes a list of permanently-banned user IDs to banned_user.cfg.", writeip, listid, say, status, users
Console Command List - Valve Developer Community (banid, removeid, say, rcon_password, hostport)
How can you Permanently ban someone? - engine usage string "banid < minutes > < userid | uniqueid > { kick }", 0 minutes = permanent, then writeid

notes: Dystopia is a free standalone Source mod and its server is plain SRCDS with the game folder "dystopia" - no mod-specific admin layer exists, so every command here is engine-level. Engine baseline is Source SDK 2013 Multiplayer: the Dystopia 1.4.1 setup guide installs app 244310 (Source SDK 2013 Server) and then the game content from app 17580 with "-beta Previous", while LinuxGSM and SteamDB use the separate dedicated-server tool app 17585, which is what game.appId records. TRANSPORT: Valve Source RCON over TCP on the same port the game uses for UDP. The guide is explicit - "-port <number> Default: 27015 ... TCP is used for RCON, UDP is used for general game traffic" - so there is no separate RCON port; -port (or hostport) moves both. There is no enable switch: RCON is live as soon as rcon_password is set in dystopia/cfg/server.cfg, which both the guide and the LinuxGSM Game-Server-Configs server.cfg do. sv_rcon_minfailures / sv_rcon_maxfailures / sv_rcon_banpenalty / sv_rcon_whitelist_address / sv_rcon_log only tune auto-banning of failed RCON logins; they do not gate RCON. LIST/INFO: status doubles as both - it prints hostname:/version:/udp/ip:/map:/players: header lines then one "#  <userid> \"<name>\" STEAM_x:y:z <connected> <ping> <loss> <state> <adr>" row per player, hence regex parsing rather than csv (names contain spaces and quotes). Some builds insert a second numeric slot column between userid and the quoted name, hence the optional group; the userid is captured as accountId because kickid also accepts it. KICK: recorded as kickid with the Steam ID. DISAGREEMENT WORTH KNOWING - the Dystopia guide documents kickid narrowly as "kickid <userid>  Kick a player from the server by UserID" and documents plain "kick <Name of player>" (case-insensitive name match) separately; the SDK 2013 engine command list this build runs on describes kickid as "Kick a player by userid or uniqueid, with a message", i.e. a Steam ID is accepted and a free-text reason is the trailing argument. kickid was chosen over kick because the Steam ID is exact where a name match is not, and because the same identifier then serves ban and unban. If a target survives a kickid by Steam ID on some older build, fall back to "kick <name>" using the name from status. Do not quote the reason - on Source the trailing message is taken as free text and quoting it is reported to break the command. BAN: the guide gives "banid <time> <SteamID or UserID of player> [kick]" - minutes first, 0 means permanent, and the optional trailing literal "kick" is what actually ejects a still-connected player; the same usage string "banid < minutes > < userid | uniqueid > { kick }" is quoted independently on the Source server forums. banid takes no reason argument, so {reason} is deliberately absent from ban. The guide also warns banid "will not work if sv_lan is set to 1". PERSISTENCE: banid and removeid change only the in-memory list. writeid rewrites dystopia/cfg/banned_user.cfg (completely overwriting it) and the server must "exec banned_user.cfg" at boot to reload it - both the guide's and LinuxGSM's server.cfg do exec banned_user.cfg / banned_ip.cfg and call writeid / writeip. So: banid, then writeid, or the ban dies at restart; removeid, then writeid, likewise. listid prints the current banned Steam IDs. IP bans use the parallel addip/removeip/writeip against banned_ip.cfg and are not mapped here because the identifier type differs. SAY: server-side "say <string>" prints to global chat as "Console" and, unlike the client-side version, includes any quotation marks literally in the printed message - so pass {message} unquoted. A known Dystopia bug crashes the server on an empty-string say, but the guide states it manifests only through the CLIENT-side say/say_team path, not server-side say; still, never send an empty {message}. MOTD: no command exists - the MOTD is the file named by the motdfile cvar (dystopia/motd.txt) - so motd is omitted rather than guessed. mp_allowvoting_kick, mp_votekick_bantime and mp_punishvotes are player-initiated votes, not admin commands, and are not mapped. Steam IDs render with universe digit 0 on some builds and 1 on others and newer builds may print the [U:1:n] form, so both are accepted. SourceMod is commonly installed on Dystopia servers and adds sm_kick/sm_ban; those are addons and are deliberately not recorded as the stock interface. Not verified against a live server. INDEPENDENT RE-CHECK 2026-09-13: confidence lowered from high to low; no command string was changed, because every one of them was re-confirmed on a primary page. The dysemjay guide really does give status, "kick - Kicks a player from the server by name. Note that the name matching is case insensitive.", "kickid - Kick a player from the server by UserID.", "banid - Ban the account specified a given SteamID or UserID for <time> minutes. If the kick argument is added, the account will also be kicked if connected.", "removeid - Remove a Steam ID from the ban list.", "writeid", "listid", say and "-port ... TCP is used for RCON, UDP is used for general game traffic". The srcds cvarlist dump and Valve's Console Command List both carry banid/removeid/listid/say/rcon_password/hostport, Valve's Source Dedicated Server page states "27015 TCP/UDP (game transmission, pings and RCON)", Valve's Rcon page states "Server must have cvar rcon_password set as non-empty string", the Game-Server-Configs Dystopia server.cfg really does carry rcon_password, exec banned_user.cfg, exec banned_ip.cfg, writeid and writeip, and the banid usage string "banid < minutes > < userid | uniqueid > { kick }" with "Use 0 minutes for permanent" is corroborated by the TF2 wiki's "banid <minutes> <steamid> - Bans a player's Steam ID for the specified number of minutes. 0 minutes is a permanent ban." TWO THINGS FAIL THE TWO-INDEPENDENT-SOURCE BAR, hence low. (1) commands.kick: only ONE source anywhere says kickid takes a Steam ID and a trailing message - the SDK 2013 cvarlist dump ("Kick a player by userid or uniqueid, with a message"). The game's own guide scopes kickid to a UserID, and neither Valve's Console Command List nor the srcds cvarlist dump contains a kickid entry at all; both describe only "kick - Kick a player by slot, userid or name." kickid {playerId} {reason} is kept because nothing contradicts it outright and banid's own "userid | uniqueid" argument wording matches, but treat it as unproven and fall back to kick with the name from status if it silently no-ops. (2) The Steam discussion at app/17580 is NOT independent evidence: it is the guide's author announcing that same GitHub guide, so it echoes source 1 rather than corroborating it. ACCOUNTID CAVEAT: on builds that print two numeric columns it is not established which is the userid, so do not feed accountId to kickid without checking a real status line. Transport, playerId, info, listPlayers, ban, unban, say and the ban-file handling are each backed by two or more independent sources and stand exactly as written.
